items.s: Enforces the MSRB’s rules against securities firms.
items.w: The MSRB has no enforcement power, so FINRA enforces its rules for securities firms.

items.s: Has rulemaking authority only and relies on other agencies to discipline violators.
items.w: The MSRB writes municipal rules but has no enforcement authority of its own.

items.s: Administers the continuing education program for the securities industry.
items.w: FINRA administers the Regulatory Element continuing education program on behalf of the industry.

items.s: Established in 1975 to govern participants in the municipal securities market.
items.w: The book states the MSRB was established in 1975 for the municipal securities market.

items.s: Runs dispute-resolution forums, including arbitration, for investors and member firms.
items.w: Administering dispute-resolution forums is one of the listed FINRA roles in the chapter.

items.s: Cannot regulate New York City as a bond issuer, only firms and professionals.
items.w: The MSRB regulates municipal securities firms and professionals, never the municipal issuers themselves.

items.s: Performs market regulation for exchanges such as Nasdaq.
items.w: Market regulation for various exchanges, including Nasdaq, is one of the listed FINRA roles.

items.s: Collects five years of residential history and ten years of employment history.
items.w: The U4 gathers background information such as address and employment history on the candidate.

items.s: Filed by the firm within 30 calendar days after a registered rep is terminated.
items.w: A firm must file the U5 with FINRA within 30 calendar days of termination.

items.s: Contains the pre-dispute arbitration agreement signed by the registered representative.
items.w: FINRA Rule 2263 requires the arbitration clause to be signed as part of the U4.

items.s: A copy must be given to the departing rep within 30 days.
items.w: The firm must give the terminated rep a copy of the U5 within 30 days.

items.s: Filed by a new employer when a long-inactive rep is hired and relicensed.
items.w: A rep returning after years away needs an original U4 filed by the hiring firm.

items.s: Must be updated when the firm learns a former rep violated securities regulations.
items.w: The firm must update the former employee’s U5 even though the person has already left.

items.s: Submitted with fingerprints and fees when a firm sponsors a new associated person.
items.w: After membership approval, the firm submits a U4, fingerprints and fees for each registered person.

items.s: Missing it makes the registration CE inactive.
items.w: Failure to complete the Regulatory Element, unlike the Firm Element, produces CE inactive status.

items.s: The firm performs an annual needs analysis and writes a training plan.
items.w: The needs analysis and written training plan are core Firm Element obligations of the broker-dealer.

items.s: Computer-based training administered by FINRA, due on or before December 31st.
items.w: FINRA administers this computer-based program with a year-end December 31st annual deadline.

items.s: Content is not defined or approved by FINRA or other regulators.
items.w: The firm’s own training plan content is not defined or approved by regulators.

items.s: The annual needs analysis weighs the size and scope of the business, products offered and customer complaints.
items.w: The firm considers these factors in its needs analysis; failure to complete the Firm Element brings discipline, not CE inactive status.

items.s: A rep may not earn new commissions while delinquent in completing it.
items.w: A CE inactive person cannot receive compensation for activities requiring registration, such as commissions.

items.s: Two years of non-completion leads to administrative termination of the registration.
items.w: After two years CE inactive, the registration is terminated and the exam must be retaken.

items.s: Deadline for fingerprints to be received after the Form U4 is filed.
items.w: Fingerprints are due within 30 days after the U4 or status becomes Inactive Prints.

items.s: A firm reports a statutory disqualifying event to FINRA on an amended U4.
items.w: Reportable events involving statutory disqualification must reach CRD within 10 calendar days.

items.s: A firm files Form U5 after a registered rep’s termination.
items.w: The U5 notice is due within 30 calendar days of termination.

items.s: Amended U4 reporting a rep’s suspension from membership in an SRO.
items.w: Suspension from an SRO is a statutory disqualification event, which must be disclosed within 10 days.

items.s: Amended U4 after a rep changes her residential address.
items.w: Normal updates such as a new address must be filed within 30 calendar days.

items.s: Amended U4 after a rep begins a paid seat on a company’s board.
items.w: An outside business activity requires an amended U4 within the normal 30 days.

items.s: Amended U4 reporting a felony conviction within the last ten years.
items.w: A felony conviction causes statutory disqualification, which must be reported within 10 calendar days.

items.s: A rep is convicted of a felony three years ago.
items.w: Felony convictions within the last 10 years cause statutory disqualification.

items.s: A rep is arrested for a felony; the case is pending with no conviction.
items.w: Arrests alone are not disqualifying; only convictions count, though compliance should be notified.

items.s: A rep is convicted of a bribery misdemeanor two years ago.
items.w: Misdemeanors involving bribery, fraud or extortion within 10 years cause statutory disqualification.

items.s: A court issues a permanent injunction against a person over unlawful investment activities.
items.w: Temporary and permanent injunctions involving unlawful investment activities disqualify at any time.

items.s: A rep legally changes her name after marriage.
items.w: A name change only requires an amended U4 and has no disqualifying effect.

items.s: The SEC finds that a person willfully violated federal securities laws.
items.w: Findings of willful violations of federal securities laws are listed disqualifying events.

items.s: A tax lien is filed against a registered rep.
items.w: A lien requires an amended U4 but is not on the statutory disqualification list.

items.s: Owes a fiduciary duty to act in the client’s best interest.
items.w: Advisers are fiduciaries because their business is providing advice to clients.

items.s: Subject to a suitability standard for all recommendations.
items.w: Broker-dealer representatives are not fiduciaries; recommendations must simply be suitable for the customer.

items.s: Typically charges a percentage of assets under management for advice.
items.w: Advisers charge for advice, typically as a percentage of assets under management.

items.s: Typically earns commissions on the transactions it executes.
items.w: Broker-dealers charge for executed transactions rather than for advice.

items.s: With over $100 million under management, files Form ADV with the SEC.
items.w: Larger advisers register with the SEC by filing Form ADV.

items.s: Advice is incidental to the main business, with no special compensation for it.
items.w: Incidental advice without special pay keeps broker-dealers and reps exempt from adviser registration.

items.s: With under $100 million under management, registers directly with each state it operates in.
items.w: Smaller advisers register with state securities commissions rather than with the SEC.
